title: Getting to the Shelter Isn't the Whole Story

body.en: Flooding has forced your community into a shared emergency shelter for the night. It's crowded, poorly lit, and you're travelling with your younger sister. What matters most for both of you right now?

choices.label: Stay together, pick a spot near an exit and near other families you know, not an isolated corner
choices.consequence: Right instinct. Emergency shelters are exactly the setting where women and girls face the highest safety risks — staying visible, together, and near people you trust measurably reduces that risk.

choices.label: Split up to each find the most comfortable spot separately
choices.consequence: Not safe. Splitting up in a crowded, poorly lit shelter removes the protection of staying together, especially for a younger sibling.

choices.label: Take the quietest, most isolated corner of the shelter for privacy
choices.consequence: Higher risk, not lower. Isolated corners in emergency shelters are exactly where safety incidents are most likely to go unnoticed — visibility is protective, not a loss of privacy worth the trade.
